newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian OTC market hit record turnover in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Croatian OTC market hit record turnover in Sept.

text.p: Croatian Varazdin over-the-counter securities market said on Wednesday it hit a record monthly turnover of 5.7 million German marks in September, overshooting a previous May record by 88.6 percent.
It said in a news release almost all traded shares, led by confectioner Kras and seaside hoteliers, made steady gains in September.
Its VIN index, reflecting strong gains in 10 most active issues, rose to 7,389 from 6,655 points. Only three of 28 traded stocks lost in value.
Of the most active, food Processor Podravka alone accounted for over 41 percent of monthly turnover. It rose 12.31 percent to 73 marks.
Hotelier stocks represented 28 percent of the total.
Kras recorded the biggest jump to 155 from 80 marks.
It was followed by four Istrian hotel firms: Istraturist, Riviera, Jadranturist and Arenaturist, rising between 62.86 and 57.78 percent to hit all-time highs.
Electric cables manufacturer Elka was the strongest gainer among industrial stocks, adding 37.50 percent to end at 55 marks.
The biggest loser was shipper Tankerska Plovidba, falling 9.09 percent to 55 marks a share.
Private Kaptol Banka, egg and chicken farm Koka and telecommunications equipment maker Ericsson Tesla traded for the first time.

Varazdin OTC market and its outpost in Osijek deal in stocks which fall short of strict Zagreb Stock Exchange listing rules as well as paid and unpaid shares in all Croatian firms undergoing privatisation.
